extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III: internal control (Annex VI) or a quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body (Annex VII).

Annex VII (notified body involvement) is mandatory for biometric identification systems (point 1 of Annex III) when harmonised standards have not been applied or fully followed, while internal control (Annex VI) may be used otherwise; for most other high-risk AI systems the internal control route under Annex VI is available.

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products already covered by EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures required by that existing legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes specified in advance for systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of a specific high-risk AI system for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII conformity assessment procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.

Annex VII section 4.5 provides that, where necessary and after other reasonable means have proven insufficient, a notified body may be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, upon a reasoned request, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts updating Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress, without needing to formally revise the AI Act itself.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.

A Council document (dated 2026) refers to AIA codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) that set the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under 'Article 30' of the Regulation, corresponding to AI systems under Annex I.A of the AI Act.

A European Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) would create a new Annex XIV listing categories and corresponding types of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) information system, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements into aviation safety rules.

As of October 2025, NANDO lists 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR), but these are MDR/IVDR designations, not AI Act designations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act according to one industry source.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states, limited capacity, and uncertain timelines, according to an industry blog.

A news blog reports that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026,' the start date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations was moved to 2 August 2029 (from a previously reported 2 December 2027), partly because harmonised standards and notified bodies were not ready.

Another source states that 'August 2026: High-risk AI obligations fully apply' is the key compliance deadline for medical device AI (SaMD) under the AI Act, with notified bodies designated under the AI Act expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments only after that date ('Post-2026').

A SaaS-focused compliance blog states that providers must issue an EU Declaration of Conformity referencing the Article 43 procedure 'before August 2, 2026,' implying continued expectation of that deadline.

For the EU Cyber Resilience Act (a separate but related regulation), zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO as of late June 2026, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027.

The original 2021 Commission proposal text of Article 43 required providers of Annex III point 1 (biometric) high-risk AI systems that applied harmonised standards or common specifications to choose one of certain listed conformity assessment procedures.

open_issues: No official EU source among those provided confirms a specific number or list of notified bodies formally designated under the AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) itself, as opposed to MDR/IVDR or CRA designations.

The relationship and status of the Commission's proposal (COM(2025) 836, 2025/0359 (COD)) establishing a new Annex XIV for NANDO is unclear — it is unclear whether this proposal has been adopted or remains pending as of the source dates.

It is unclear from the sources whether the 'Article 30' notified body reference in the Council document (source 8) is a drafting/numbering inconsistency with Article 43/Article 35 of the adopted AI Act, or refers to a different proposed instrument.

The true legal status and date of the claimed shift of the Annex III deadline to 2 August 2029 (source 15) is not corroborated by any official EU source and conflicts with other sources assuming an August 2026 deadline; it remains unresolved which date is currently legally operative.
The sources do not specify how many AI Act notified bodies, if any, have been designated as of October 2026 (the current date), nor which Member States or sectors they cover.

The interplay between MDR/IVDR notified body designations and separate AI Act-specific notified body designation for medical device AI (SaMD) is not fully clarified — sources indicate overlap but no confirmed joint designations.
The impact of the Cyber Resilience Act's notified body delays (source 20) on the AI Act's notified body ecosystem, if any, is not addressed by the sources.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the State of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control and notified-body assessment — with the latter mandatory in specific circumstances such as certain biometric systems and products already regulated under other EU harmonisation legislation (high confidence). However, the notified body ecosystem required to implement these assessments remains underdeveloped and possibly delayed, with no official EU source confirming any AI Act-specific notified body designations as of the latest available documents (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out two conformity assessment paths for Annex III high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or a combination of quality management system review plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Power Quant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For most high-risk categories the internal-control route is available, but Annex VII notified-body involvement becomes mandatory for biometric identification systems (Annex III, point 1) when harmonised standards have not been applied or fully followed (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

Where a high-risk AI system is a safety component of a product already covered by EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sector's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes specified in advance for systems designed to keep learning after deployment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise a specific high-risk system's placement on the market for a limited period, by derogation from Article 43, for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

Providers generally may select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the system is intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43 – GA](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII section 4.5 allows notified bodies, as a last resort and under IP/confidentiality safeguards, to access training data and trained models upon reasoned request (medium confidence) ([Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). The Commission retains power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts without a full legislative revision (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Framework and Status
Article 35 of the AI Act establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A 2026 Council document references "AIP 0101–0105" codes defining designation scope for bodies notified under what it calls "Article 30," corresponding to Annex I.A product systems — though it is unclear whether this is a drafting inconsistency (medium confidence) ([Council ST-7322-2026](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV listing AI system categories for the NANDO information system and integrate AI Act requirements into aviation safety rules, though its adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council ST-15708-2025](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

As of October 2025, NANDO lists 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation — but these are MDR/IVDR, not AI Act, designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex SWD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). One industry source states that as of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act itself (low confidence) ([AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A separate industry source, as of March 2026, describes the AI Act notified body designation process as still being built out across member states amid capacity constraints and uncertain timelines, but does not itself confirm a zero count of designations (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on the operative Annex III high-risk deadline: most assume obligations apply from August 2026, while one unverified news blog claims a "final text" from September 2026 postponed the deadline to 2 August 2029 due to unready standards and notified bodies (low confidence, below 0.4) ([SOTA.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026), [AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). This 2029 date is not corroborated by any official EU source and should be treated with strong caution. Sources also present slightly differing pictures of the 2026 designation landscape: one explicitly asserts zero AI Act designations as of April 2026, while the other merely describes an ongoing, nascent process as of March 2026 without making a zero-count claim — these are not strictly contradictory but reflect varying levels of specificity (both low confidence) ([AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). The related Cyber Resilience Act also shows zero notified body designations as of June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)), suggesting a broader pattern of delayed EU conformity-assessment infrastructure, though this is not directly tied to the AI Act.

## Knowledge Gaps
No official EU source confirms a specific number or list of bodies formally designated as AI Act notified bodies. The legal status of COM(2025) 836's proposed Annex XIV/NANDO integration is unresolved. The "Article 30" reference in the 2026 Council document is unexplained and may reflect numbering confusion. # Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the State of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control and notified-body assessment — with the latter mandatory in specific circumstances such as certain biometric systems and products already regulated under other EU harmonisation legislation (high confidence). However, the notified body ecosystem required to implement these assessments remains underdeveloped and possibly delayed, with no official EU source confirming any AI Act-specific notified body designations as of the latest available documents (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out two conformity assessment paths for Annex III high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or a combination of quality management system review plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Power Quant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For most high-risk categories the internal-control route is available, but Annex VII notified-body involvement becomes mandatory for biometric identification systems (Annex III, point 1) when harmonised standards have not been applied or fully followed (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

Where a high-risk AI system is a safety component of a product already covered by EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sector's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes specified in advance for systems designed to keep learning after deployment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise a specific high-risk system's placement on the market for a limited period, by derogation from Article 43, for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

Providers generally may select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the system is intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43 – GA](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII section 4.5 allows notified bodies, as a last resort and under IP/confidentiality safeguards, to access training data and trained models upon reasoned request (medium confidence) ([Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). The Commission retains power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts without a full legislative revision (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Framework and Status
Article 35 of the AI Act establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A 2026 Council document references "AIP 0101–0105" codes defining designation scope for bodies notified under what it calls "Article 30," corresponding to Annex I.A product systems — though it is unclear whether this is a drafting inconsistency (medium confidence) ([Council ST-7322-2026](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV listing AI system categories for the NANDO information system and integrate AI Act requirements into aviation safety rules, though its adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council ST-15708-2025](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

As of October 2025, NANDO lists 51 notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation — but these are MDR/IVDR, not AI Act, designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex SWD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Industry sources report that as of April–March 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act itself, with the designation ecosystem still being built across member states amid capacity constraints (low confidence) ([AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on the operative Annex III high-risk deadline: most assume obligations apply from August 2026, while one unverified news blog claims a "final text" from September 2026 postponed the deadline to 2 August 2029 due to unready standards and notified bodies (low confidence, below 0.4) ([SOTA.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026), [AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). This 2029 date is not corroborated by any official EU source and should be treated with strong caution. Sources also vary slightly on the 2026 designation picture — one asserts zero designations as of April 2026 while another simply describes an ongoing, nascent process (both low confidence) ([AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). The related Cyber Resilience Act also shows zero notified body designations as of June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)), suggesting a broader pattern of delayed EU conformity-assessment infrastructure, though this is not directly tied to the AI Act.

## Knowledge Gaps
No official EU source confirms a specific number or list of bodies formally designated as AI Act notified bodies. The legal status of COM(2025) 836's proposed Annex XIV/NANDO integration is unresolved. The "Article 30" reference in the 2026 Council document is unexplained and may reflect numbering confusion. The true operative Annex III deadline (2026 vs. 2029) remains unconfirmed by primary sources. Finally, the interplay between MDR/IVDR notified bodies and AI Act-specific designations for medical device AI remains unclarified.
